entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New in v2.7.0 ("doc-rot doors — impact, routing, doc-deferral, freshness", released 2026-08-16; features `knowledge-distill-trigger` + `doc-impact-synthesis`, landed 2026-08-03→2026-08-16 — did not exist at the v1.18.3 cursor). Four HARD doors block a feature's close, run after tests/scribing-debt/judge-debt/pattern-check: **(1) knowledge-freshness** — blocks on any `dangling_source`/`dangling_required_context` warning inside the feature's own touched areas (`bee knowledge check`'s findings, scope-filtered — a sibling feature's stale pointers never tax this close). **(2) impact** — blocks when a doc still cites one of the closing feature's OWN decisions "without having been reconciled": collects the feature's decide events by structured `feature` field, sweeps `docs/**` for citations of each id, blocks on every surviving hit with file:line + remedy, re-runs fresh each close so a fixed doc self-clears. **(3) routing** — blocks when a locked D-ID in the feature's own CONTEXT.md decision table has **no area-spec citation AND no feature-local record** — i.e. a locked local decision that was never propagated into any durable doc is refused at close, not allowed to rot as an orphaned CONTEXT.md-only fact. **(4) doc-deferral** — blocks when deferral-shaped prose ("later", "TODO"-style postponement) in touched docs names no registered trigger in the two-tier trigger registry (`bee triggers add/list/resolve`; predicate-tier auto-flips `waiting→due` on a re-evaluated condition, manual-tier needs human confirm). Each door has a named, logged escape hatch (`knowledge-freshness-deferral` / `impact-deferral` / `routing-deferral` / `doc-deferral` decision) — never a silent skip.

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New system since v1.18.3, `docs/knowledge/areas/decision-memory/overview.md` (9 business rules). Decisions carry a global content-hash `short8` id (never a small integer alone); **R8 — Citation discipline (D3):** any artifact encoding a decision cites that short8 id, which is what makes reversal reachable. **R2 — a supersede is not finished until every citing artifact is reconciled:** before its single log append, `decisions supersede` computes a citation sweep over `docs/**` (full id + word-boundary short8 match); every hit is fixed same-turn or explicitly waived with a recorded reason, and an unreconciled hit resurfaces at every flush. `decisions log --relation touches:<id>` runs the same sweep for a non-superseding reference. Free text that reads as an inline supersession claim ("supersedes", "replaces", "no longer applies"...) is refused unless a real `--relation supersedes:<id>` resolves it — a guard added after a store audit found 70 decide events hiding a supersession in prose against 29 proper supersede events. **R5 — the recall surface is a machine-regenerated index** (`docs/decisions/index.md`, never hand-edited, grouped scope→tag, superseded entries excluded, byte-stable, "complete by construction"), with structured search (`--tag`, `--scope`, `--since`, `--untagged`) — "bare substring grep is the fallback, never the recall path."

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New in v2.7.0 ("doc-rot doors — impact, routing, doc-deferral, freshness", released 2026-08-16; features `knowledge-distill-trigger` + `doc-impact-synthesis`, landed 2026-08-03→2026-08-16 — did not exist at the v1.18.3 cursor). Four HARD doors block a feature's close, run after tests/scribing-debt/judge-debt/pattern-check: **(1) knowledge-freshness** — blocks on any `dangling_source`/`dangling_required_context` warning inside the feature's own touched areas (`bee knowledge check`'s findings, scope-filtered — a sibling feature's stale pointers never tax this close). **(2) impact** — blocks when a doc still cites one of the closing feature's OWN decisions "without having been reconciled": collects the feature's decide events by structured `feature` field, sweeps `docs/**` for citations of each id, blocks on every surviving hit with file:line + remedy, re-runs fresh each close so a fixed doc self-clears. **(3) routing** — blocks when a locked D-ID in the feature's own CONTEXT.md decision table has **no area-spec citation AND no feature-local record** — i.e. a locked local decision that was never propagated into any durable doc is refused at close, not allowed to rot as an orphaned CONTEXT.md-only fact. **(4) doc-deferral** — blocks when deferral-shaped prose ("later", "TODO"-style postponement) in touched docs names no registered trigger in the two-tier trigger registry (`bee triggers add/list/resolve`; predicate-tier auto-flips `waiting→due` on a re-evaluated condition, manual-tier needs human confirm). Each door has a named, logged escape hatch (`knowledge-freshness-deferral` / `impact-deferral` / `routing-deferral` / `doc-deferral` decision) — never a silent skip.

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New system since v1.18.3, `docs/knowledge/areas/decision-memory/overview.md` (9 business rules). Decisions carry a global content-hash `short8` id (never a small integer alone); **R8 — Citation discipline (D3):** any artifact encoding a decision cites that short8 id, which is what makes reversal reachable. **R2 — a supersede is not finished until every citing artifact is reconciled:** before its single log append, `decisions supersede` computes a citation sweep over `docs/**` (full id + word-boundary short8 match); every hit is fixed same-turn or explicitly waived with a recorded reason, and an unreconciled hit resurfaces at every flush. `decisions log --relation touches:<id>` runs the same sweep for a non-superseding reference. Free text that reads as an inline supersession claim ("supersedes", "replaces", "no longer applies"...) is refused unless a real `--relation supersedes:<id>` resolves it — a guard added after a store audit found 70 decide events hiding a supersession in prose against 29 proper supersede events. **R5 — the recall surface is a machine-regenerated index** (`docs/decisions/index.md`, never hand-edited, grouped scope→tag, superseded entries excluded, byte-stable, "complete by construction"), with structured search (`--tag`, `--scope`, `--since`, `--untagged`) — "bare substring grep is the fallback, never the recall path."

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New in v2.7.0 ("doc-rot doors — impact, routing, doc-deferral, freshness", released 2026-08-16; features `knowledge-distill-trigger` + `doc-impact-synthesis`, landed 2026-08-03→2026-08-16 — did not exist at the v1.18.3 cursor). Four HARD doors block a feature's close, run after tests/scribing-debt/judge-debt/pattern-check: **(1) knowledge-freshness** — blocks on any `dangling_source`/`dangling_required_context` warning inside the feature's own touched areas (`bee knowledge check`'s findings, scope-filtered — a sibling feature's stale pointers never tax this close). **(2) impact** — blocks when a doc still cites one of the closing feature's OWN decisions "without having been reconciled": collects the feature's decide events by structured `feature` field, sweeps `docs/**` for citations of each id, blocks on every surviving hit with file:line + remedy, re-runs fresh each close so a fixed doc self-clears. **(3) routing** — blocks when a locked D-ID in the feature's own CONTEXT.md decision table has **no area-spec citation AND no feature-local record** — i.e. a locked local decision that was never propagated into any durable doc is refused at close, not allowed to rot as an orphaned CONTEXT.md-only fact. **(4) doc-deferral** — blocks when deferral-shaped prose ("later", "TODO"-style postponement) in touched docs names no registered trigger in the two-tier trigger registry (`bee triggers add/list/resolve`; predicate-tier auto-flips `waiting→due` on a re-evaluated condition, manual-tier needs human confirm). Each door has a named, logged escape hatch (`knowledge-freshness-deferral` / `impact-deferral` / `routing-deferral` / `doc-deferral` decision) — never a silent skip.

Inputs that live in the hidden run state (`unit-run:` and `gate-answer:` inputs, a panel synthesizer's panelist reports) reach each blind role as byte-identical copies in `inputs/` of its own assignment directory, neutral names (`seat-A`) with `anonymizeInputs`; a source that changed since it settled refuses the unit. The `delphi`, `nominal-group` and `group-cognition` panel steps that must not see each other run blind. Check readiness with the `confinement-blind-read` row of `fgos doctor`. entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: **Vai mù thật sự (`blind`) — chặn đọc run state của peer.** Mặc định tắt (không đổi hành vi). Một cờ ở Unit (và ở `template` của Workflow): `blind: true` làm *mọi vai* của Unit chạy với `hostRead: blind` (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §9.2): worker không đọc được `.fgos/assignments`, `.fgos/workflow-runs`, `.fgos/dispatch-runs` của project, thư mục socket herdr, private home của dispatch khác, hay `/proc/<pid>` của tiến trình anh em; chỉ đọc được thư mục của chính nó (brief, ref đã được trao — chỉ-đọc) và ghi outbox. Phần còn lại của host (repo, `node`, DNS) và file tracked trong `.fgos` không đổi. Unit `blind` không bao giờ chạy không-blind: nếu không thực thi được — `bind()` không chọn in-process/inline, không có bwrap, mode không `required`, probe hỏng/chưa tươi, `cwd` hay ref nằm trong vùng bị che — dispatch bị từ chối trước khi spawn với lý do có tên (`blind-in-process`, `blind-requires-confinement`, `blind-hides-workspace`, `blind-ref-hidden`, `confinement-probe-failed`, ...). Với Unit `blind`, input `unit-run:`/`gate-answer:` (và ref bất kỳ nằm trong vùng bị che) không được giao bằng đường dẫn gốc: lúc dispatch, `resolveUnitInputs` + `copyHandoffsInto` chép nguyên byte (kiểm sha256) vào `inputs/` của round dir của chính vai đó, mỗi vai một bản, tên trung tính khi có `anonymizeInputs`; `unit.json` giữ `inputMap`, resume dùng lại bản chép. `blind-ref-hidden` chỉ còn cho ref không chép được. Workflow bật `blind`: hai bước panel của `delphi` (`propose-round-1`, `propose-round-2`), `generate-ideas` của `nominal-group`, `sense-making-panel` của `group-cognition`, `shaping` của `architecture-advisory` (`core/workflows/architecture-advisory.yaml`) và `perspectives` của `business-discussion` (`core/workflows/business-discussion.yaml`).

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute <id> --for <capability>` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor.<id>.agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities.<name>.prefer`). The CLI door `execute <agent>` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute <agent> --for <capability>` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract <file> --executor <id>` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "<prompt>" --provider <id>` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider.

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: `install.ps1` installs `fgctl.exe` into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\fgos\bin` (or `FGCTL_INSTALL_DIR`) and prints, without running, the commands that put that directory on `PATH`. Like `install.sh` it takes the latest NON-prerelease unless `FGCTL_VERSION` names a tag, so a pre-release such as `v0.2.0-rc.2` needs `FGCTL_VERSION`. `fgctl init` then downloads the `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` asset through the `curl.exe` that ships with Windows, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS`, and writes the workspace launchers: `.fgos/installation/bin/fgos.cmd` and `fgos-runner.cmd` for PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, beside the `sh` pair for Git Bash. A release publishes the same asset set for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` (built on `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate that its binaries need no glibc newer than 2.35) and `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`; macOS is not published. The full rule is RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell) in `docs/specs/distribution.md`.

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: | 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: | 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - `src/state/` — lõi work-state: events (nhật ký; `appendEvent` nay chạy trong mutex nóng `state` (`withStateTx`, `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`) — xem spec Work-State RUL10 (tiền đề có ngưỡng — một người ghi tại một thời điểm; multi-agent ghi đồng thời qua mutex nóng `state`)), work (schema — STATUSES + STAGES + field `parent` lineage + field `domain`), fsm (bảng chuyển status + CAS), stage (bảng chuyển stage + CAS, chiều vĩ mô song song fsm; cạnh chuyển-stage tra theo domain của item — `coding`: `discovery → exploring → planning → executing`, trong đó phán-quyết `clear` ở `discovery` bỏ qua `exploring` để sang thẳng `planning` còn `unclear` đi qua `exploring`; tên `decompose` vẫn còn nhưng chỉ là bí danh legacy chỉ-để-rút-cạn (không việc MỚI nào vào được nữa); `synthetic`: một stage, không cạnh nào), domains (sổ đăng ký domain — stage list + step-mapping base-workflow + cạnh-chuyển mỗi domain; `coding` + ba domain minh họa/thử-nghiệm `synthetic` (đúng một stage), `triage`, `fixture-marketing`; base-workflow-model STR18, hoàn tất S1+S2), replay (fold), frontier (truy vấn sẵn-sàng — lọc theo status, stage domain-aware, VÀ lineage qua `parent`), dep-graph (dò chu trình trên `deps` — bất biến phi-chu-trình tại cửa ghi, per work-graph-intelligence S1), store (chủ ghi duy nhất + readRawEvents), envelope (phong bì output CTR001, `wrapEnvelope` — nay bọc MỌI verb ở một cửa in trong `bin/fgos.mjs main()`, STR37; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §envelope)

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New system since v1.18.3, `docs/knowledge/areas/decision-memory/overview.md` (9 business rules). Decisions carry a global content-hash `short8` id (never a small integer alone); **R8 — Citation discipline (D3):** any artifact encoding a decision cites that short8 id, which is what makes reversal reachable. **R2 — a supersede is not finished until every citing artifact is reconciled:** before its single log append, `decisions supersede` computes a citation sweep over `docs/**` (full id + word-boundary short8 match); every hit is fixed same-turn or explicitly waived with a recorded reason, and an unreconciled hit resurfaces at every flush. `decisions log --relation touches:<id>` runs the same sweep for a non-superseding reference. Free text that reads as an inline supersession claim ("supersedes", "replaces", "no longer applies"...) is refused unless a real `--relation supersedes:<id>` resolves it — a guard added after a store audit found 70 decide events hiding a supersession in prose against 29 proper supersede events. **R5 — the recall surface is a machine-regenerated index** (`docs/decisions/index.md`, never hand-edited, grouped scope→tag, superseded entries excluded, byte-stable, "complete by construction"), with structured search (`--tag`, `--scope`, `--since`, `--untagged`) — "bare substring grep is the fallback, never the recall path."

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New in v2.7.0 ("doc-rot doors — impact, routing, doc-deferral, freshness", released 2026-08-16; features `knowledge-distill-trigger` + `doc-impact-synthesis`, landed 2026-08-03→2026-08-16 — did not exist at the v1.18.3 cursor). Four HARD doors block a feature's close, run after tests/scribing-debt/judge-debt/pattern-check: **(1) knowledge-freshness** — blocks on any `dangling_source`/`dangling_required_context` warning inside the feature's own touched areas (`bee knowledge check`'s findings, scope-filtered — a sibling feature's stale pointers never tax this close). **(2) impact** — blocks when a doc still cites one of the closing feature's OWN decisions "without having been reconciled": collects the feature's decide events by structured `feature` field, sweeps `docs/**` for citations of each id, blocks on every surviving hit with file:line + remedy, re-runs fresh each close so a fixed doc self-clears. **(3) routing** — blocks when a locked D-ID in the feature's own CONTEXT.md decision table has **no area-spec citation AND no feature-local record** — i.e. a locked local decision that was never propagated into any durable doc is refused at close, not allowed to rot as an orphaned CONTEXT.md-only fact. **(4) doc-deferral** — blocks when deferral-shaped prose ("later", "TODO"-style postponement) in touched docs names no registered trigger in the two-tier trigger registry (`bee triggers add/list/resolve`; predicate-tier auto-flips `waiting→due` on a re-evaluated condition, manual-tier needs human confirm). Each door has a named, logged escape hatch (`knowledge-freshness-deferral` / `impact-deferral` / `routing-deferral` / `doc-deferral` decision) — never a silent skip.

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New system since v1.18.3, `docs/knowledge/areas/decision-memory/overview.md` (9 business rules). Decisions carry a global content-hash `short8` id (never a small integer alone); **R8 — Citation discipline (D3):** any artifact encoding a decision cites that short8 id, which is what makes reversal reachable. **R2 — a supersede is not finished until every citing artifact is reconciled:** before its single log append, `decisions supersede` computes a citation sweep over `docs/**` (full id + word-boundary short8 match); every hit is fixed same-turn or explicitly waived with a recorded reason, and an unreconciled hit resurfaces at every flush. `decisions log --relation touches:<id>` runs the same sweep for a non-superseding reference. Free text that reads as an inline supersession claim ("supersedes", "replaces", "no longer applies"...) is refused unless a real `--relation supersedes:<id>` resolves it — a guard added after a store audit found 70 decide events hiding a supersession in prose against 29 proper supersede events. **R5 — the recall surface is a machine-regenerated index** (`docs/decisions/index.md`, never hand-edited, grouped scope→tag, superseded entries excluded, byte-stable, "complete by construction"), with structured search (`--tag`, `--scope`, `--since`, `--untagged`) — "bare substring grep is the fallback, never the recall path."

entries.sourceLineAtOldCoordinate: - **What:** New in v2.7.0 ("doc-rot doors — impact, routing, doc-deferral, freshness", released 2026-08-16; features `knowledge-distill-trigger` + `doc-impact-synthesis`, landed 2026-08-03→2026-08-16 — did not exist at the v1.18.3 cursor). Four HARD doors block a feature's close, run after tests/scribing-debt/judge-debt/pattern-check: **(1) knowledge-freshness** — blocks on any `dangling_source`/`dangling_required_context` warning inside the feature's own touched areas (`bee knowledge check`'s findings, scope-filtered — a sibling feature's stale pointers never tax this close). **(2) impact** — blocks when a doc still cites one of the closing feature's OWN decisions "without having been reconciled": collects the feature's decide events by structured `feature` field, sweeps `docs/**` for citations of each id, blocks on every surviving hit with file:line + remedy, re-runs fresh each close so a fixed doc self-clears. **(3) routing** — blocks when a locked D-ID in the feature's own CONTEXT.md decision table has **no area-spec citation AND no feature-local record** — i.e. a locked local decision that was never propagated into any durable doc is refused at close, not allowed to rot as an orphaned CONTEXT.md-only fact. **(4) doc-deferral** — blocks when deferral-shaped prose ("later", "TODO"-style postponement) in touched docs names no registered trigger in the two-tier trigger registry (`bee triggers add/list/resolve`; predicate-tier auto-flips `waiting→due` on a re-evaluated condition, manual-tier needs human confirm). Each door has a named, logged escape hatch (`knowledge-freshness-deferral` / `impact-deferral` / `routing-deferral` / `doc-deferral` decision) — never a silent skip.
